title: Finite-quotient coefficient and localized ordinary pullback normalization
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$, and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X''\xrightarrow hX'\xrightarrow gX$ be morphisms of noetherian finite-dimensional schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. Use their small pro-etale sites and canonical inverse images [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. For $W=X,X',X''$, put $B_W=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_W$, with projections $\pi_{W,n}$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum], and $E_W=B_W[1/\varpi]$ [def-weil-pbc-ringed-section-localization]. Use module sheaves, sheaf tensor products and ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a morphism $u:V\to W$, let $d_{u,n}:u^{-1}(A/\varpi^n)_W\to(A/\varpi^n)_V$ be the canonical constant-section map and $c_u:u^{-1}B_W\to B_V$ the map with components $d_{u,n}u^{-1}\pi_{W,n}$ [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. Set $P_u=B_V\otimes^L_{u^{-1}B_W}u^{-1}(-)$, with canonical ordinary composition $a:P_hP_g\xrightarrow\sim P_{g\circ h}$ and identity $e:P_{\mathrm{id}}\xrightarrow\sim\mathrm{id}$ [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Set $F_W=E_W\otimes^L_{B_W}(-)$ and $G_u=E_V\otimes^L_{u^{-1}E_W}u^{-1}(-)$. In defining these functors use the canonical localization-unit comparison $u^{-1}E_W\cong(u^{-1}B_W)[1/\varpi]$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-inverse-image-coherence]. Let $\delta_u:F_VP_u\xrightarrow\sim G_uF_W$ be the balanced comparison through $E_V\otimes^L_{u^{-1}B_W}u^{-1}(-)$, whose inverse inserts the coefficient unit; let $b:G_hG_g\xrightarrow\sim G_{g\circ h}$ and $e_E:G_{\mathrm{id}}\xrightarrow\sim\mathrm{id}$ be the ordinary rational comparisons.
Then $d_{g\circ h,n}=d_{h,n}h^{-1}(d_{g,n})$ and $c_{g\circ h}=c_hh^{-1}(c_g)$ under the canonical inverse-image composition isomorphism $(g\circ h)^{-1}\cong h^{-1}g^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition]. In particular
$$\pi_{X'',n}c_hh^{-1}c_g=d_{h,n}h^{-1}d_{g,n}h^{-1}g^{-1}\pi_{X,n}=\pi_{X'',n}c_{g\circ h}.$$
These equalities respect quotient transitions; the identity maps are the canonical identities and all maps fix the constant scalar $\varpi$.
For every $K\in D(B_X)$ one has the equality of specified natural transformations
$$\delta_{g\circ h,K}F_{X''}(a_K)=b_{F_XK}\,G_h(\delta_{g,K})\,\delta_{h,P_gK},\qquad e_E\delta_{\mathrm{id}}=F(e).$$
On flat-term K-flat representatives [def-pc-kflat-complex] the two composition maps, after the canonical tensor identifications, both send $e''\otimes b'\otimes k$ to $e''\iota_{X''}(c_h(b'))\otimes k$, where $\iota_W:B_W\to E_W$ is localization. The underlying balanced maps commute with restrictions and differentials and give this equality in the derived category, naturally for every derived $K$. The rational compositor $b$ sends $e''\otimes e'\otimes k$ to $e''d_h^E(e')\otimes k$, where $d_h^E:h^{-1}E_{X'}\to E_{X''}$ is the localized coefficient map; its inverse inserts $1$. The identity comparison multiplies the scalar into the module. No structural coefficient map is assumed invertible.
